product.schneider-towerat220-mega.summar: The limited 220 edition that doubles memory and adopts high-density floppies.
product.schneider-towerat220-mega.histor: Happy Computer presented Tower AT 220 Mega in May 1989 as an announced run of 2,000 units. It cost nearly 3,800 DM with a monochrome monitor, about 300 DM above the standard 220. It kept the 20 MB disk while expanding memory and floppy capacity, updating the same DOS and Works working package.
product.schneider-towerat220-mega.techni: Memory and floppy capacity distinguish the edition. The magazine documents 1 MB and 1.44 MB versus the standard 220's 512 KB and 720 KB; it also quotes about 4,600 DM with EGA and nearly 5,300 DM with a multisync monitor. The production run was announced, not independently verified.
The Mega label does not identify a unique BIOS. No pair is specifically attributed to the 220 Mega in the reviewed records; MAME's cited BIOS 1.07 came from a 240 Mega, a different model.
product.schneider-towerat220-mega.warnin: Historical sheet under research; booting in BluMach remains unvalidated.
product.schneider-towerat220-mega.techni: Sources and file hashes have been checked. BluMach a1b0125d has no dedicated entry for this model; MAME groups Tower AT 2xx machines as not working. Booting has not been tested.
The complete machine still needs validation. Board, BIOS pair and video ROM must be identified, then POST, memory, keyboard, RTC, disks and ports tested before usable emulation can be claimed.
A shared case does not guarantee the same board. The preserved manual covers 201/202/220; its architecture guides research, but schematics and revisions for this variant still need comparison.
Schneider, Service Manual Tower AT 201/202/220, Ident-Nr. 44657, 03/1989: cover and CPU/memory diagrams reviewed; PDF preserved.
Happy Computer 11/1988, M. Ohnesorg/rz, Rechengiganten zu Niedrigpreisen, pp. 97–98 and 101: review of a Tower AT without a hard disk, with no commercial suffix identified.
Happy Computer 05/1989, Sammlerstück, p. 18: 220 Mega edition, equipment, prices and announced production run; scan and transcription preserved.
Jungsi, Schneider VGA AT System 40: range overview and approximate chronology; not a substitute for a manual covering each revision.
MAME, at.cpp: towerat2xx sets, variant provenance and unresolved EGA pairings. Files are preserved in the library; their presence does not prove universal compatibility.
BluMach a1b0125d, inspected and preserved machine table: no dedicated Tower AT entry.
